key_insight: An NLP pipeline that reads both the Findings and Impressions sections of radiology reports can identify brain metastases at scale, including cases not captured by cancer registries.
clinical_relevance: This could improve population-level surveillance of brain metastases and help registries better track asynchronous disease burden across health systems.
method: Trained two Bio_ClinicalBERT models separately on Findings and Impressions text.
Combined the two section-level predictions by taking the maximum probability as the report-level label.
Validated the system on internal and external reports from Alberta, Ontario, and British Columbia.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1,879 samples and in internal validation reached 0.888 sensitivity at a 0.4 threshold, with external sensitivity of 0.918 in Ontario and 0.726 in British Columbia.
watch_item: Performance varied by province, so local data differences and threshold selection may affect real-world deployment.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
